comments.note: AICacheLocation uses a private constructor + singleton getInstance() pattern, which prevents direct instantiation. APIResponseCacheLocation uses no constructor at all (stateless, fully delegates to static APICacheManager). The difference is intentional since APIResponseCacheLocation has no state to protect — but the two patterns are inconsistent across cache locations. Consider documenting the preferred instantiation style in a coding convention.

RegisterAPIResponseCacheListener::getCacheLocations() creates a new APIResponseCacheLocation() on every call. Since the object is stateless and cheap to construct this is harmless, but it's inconsistent with RegisterAPIIndexCacheListener which returns a cached instance via APIManager::getInstance()->getMethodIndex()->getCacheLocation(). No change needed, but worth noting.

No dedicated unit tests exist for APIResponseCacheLocation or RegisterAPIResponseCacheListener. These should be added once the vendor environment is restored. The integration test for the full caching pipeline (WP plan step 12) should cover the getByteSize() and clear() acceptance criteria in an end-to-end test.

comments.note: RegisterAPIResponseCacheListener::getCacheLocations() creates new APIResponseCacheLocation() on every call, while RegisterAPIIndexCacheListener retrieves a cached instance from APIManager. The difference is intentional: APIResponseCacheLocation is stateless and has no owning manager to retrieve from. A short inline comment explaining the design choice (e.g., '// Stateless object — direct instantiation is correct') would help future readers who notice the inconsistency with the sibling class.

@package / @subpackage annotations are inconsistent between the two listeners in the same directory: RegisterAPIResponseCacheListener uses '@package API / @subpackage Events'; RegisterAPIIndexCacheListener uses '@package Application / @subpackage CacheControl'. Both are in namespace Application\API\Events. Not functionally impactful, but aligning them to a common standard would improve consistency. The framework convention check would clarify which is correct.

No observations on APIResponseCacheLocation or RegisterAPIResponseCacheListener — both are clean, minimal, and follow the established pattern precisely. LOCATION_ID constant is a good touch enabling reference-free string coupling.
